Question Explanation: $\text{HI}$ cleavage of a cyclic diether.

Concept: Cleavage of Ethers (vicinal).

 

Solution: The reactant is a cyclic diether (1,3-Benzodioxane or Chroman-2-one derivative). Cleavage with $\mathbf{\text{HI}}$ (excess) and heat ($\mathbf{\Delta}$) will cleave all $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bonds that are not aryl-oxygen bonds.

  1. The $\text{C}-\text{O}_{\text{aryl}}$ bond is strong due to resonance, so the $\text{O}-\text{C}_{\text{alkyl}}$ bonds (both are $\mathbf{1^\circ}$ benzylic $\text{C}$ atoms) cleave. The initial product of double cleavage is a diol and an alkyl halide.

    • The two $\text{O}$ atoms are replaced by $\text{OH}$ groups (initially forming a diol) and the alkyl bridge ($\text{CH}_2$) is cleaved.

    • The two $\text{O}-\text{CH}_2$ bonds cleave, yielding Catechol ($\mathbf{1,2\text{-dihydroxybenzene}}$) and two $\text{CH}_2\text{I}$ groups.

  2. The product of the ether cleavage is a diol with two $\text{OH}$ groups adjacent to each other on the aromatic ring and a $\text{CH}_2\text{I}$ group at the ortho position, depending on the exact structure.

Assuming the structure is $\text{1,2-Methylenedioxybenzene}$ (an acetal), the product is $\text{Catechol} + \text{CH}_2\text{I}_2$ (Methylene iodide).

Given the structure is a cyclic acetal ($\mathbf{1,2\text{-Methylenedioxybenzene}}$) based on the $\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{(OCH}_2\text{O)}$ structure:

$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{(OCH}_2\text{O)} + 4\text{HI} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathbf{\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{(OH)}_2} + \mathbf{\text{CH}_2\text{I}_2} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

The products are Catechol ($\mathbf{1,2\text{-dihydroxybenzene}}$) and Methylene iodide ($\mathbf{\text{CH}_2\text{I}_2}$).

Matching the options: Option 1 shows $\text{Catechol}$ ($\text{o}\text{-dihydroxybenzene}$) and $\mathbf{\text{CH}_2\text{I}_2}$.

 

Final Answer: $+\text{CH}_2\text{I}_2$"
